correctness.rationale: For H² and f=c∏(z−ζ_j)^{m_j} with ≥2 fixed distinct unit-circle nodes and at least one repeated zero, polynomial residual R=1−fq_n has exact Euler jet constraints (E^ℓR)(ζ_j)=δ_(ℓ,0). Evaluation matrix A_(jℓ),k=k^ℓ ζ_j^k for k=0..K−1 (K=n+d+1) has full row rank by Hermite interpolation; min-norm coefficients equal a=A*(AA*)^(−1)b. Scaling its Gram by D_K,jℓ=K^(ℓ+1/2) yields block diag H_(m_j) plus O_f(K^−1): diagonal Hilbert moment blocks from Riemann sums and cross-node oscillatory sums O(K^(ℓ+v)) by summation by parts. Positive block inverse perturbation gives K||a||²=Σ(H_m^(−1))_00+O_f(K^−1). The Hilbert inverse first column is the shifted-Legendre evaluation-at-zero reproducer Q_m(t)=Σ_(ν<m)(2ν+1)(−1)^νP_ν(2t−1), with Q_m(0)=m²; thus ||a||²=(Σm_j²)/K+O_f(K^−2) and the simultaneous all-index profile Ka_k=Σconjζ_j^k Q_(m_j)(k/K)+O_f(K^−1). Independent exact Hilbert inverse first entries 1,4,9,16 (m=1..4) and normalized finite mixed-multiplicity Gram residuals converge toward 5 and13. Uniformity is in 0≤k<K with fixed nodes, not coalescing nodes.

value.rationale: Repeated boundary zeros control inverse-filter approximation difficulty; the leading constant is quadratic in multiplicities rather than linear, and the result identifies the complete shape of every residual coefficient with explicit Legendre profiles. This gives a natural sharp quantitative extension of simple-root Hardy approximation.

limitations: Distinct fixed unit-circle zeros, fixed multiplicities and unweighted H². Implicit constants depend on the nodes; no uniformity under merging zeros.
